# Authoring a Betta plugin

Betta (`Betta.gha`, loaded by Rhino) reflects over attributed C# types and publishes real GH components. Write a plain service; no `GH_Component` subclass, no manual wiring. Drop to raw GH only for custom canvas UI, data-tree access, or non-standard param behavior.

## The contract

A "collection" is any type inheriting **`IBettaCollection`** (the opt-in marker; without it the type is silently skipped) whose **public** methods carry `[GrasshopperMethod]`.

- **Class-direct (terse):** `public class MyPack : IBettaCollection` + `[GrasshopperCollection(category, subCategory)]`, attributes on its own public methods.
- **Interface-based:** attributes on `public interface IMyPack : IBettaCollection`, implemented by a separate class (Betta auto-binds it in DI). Use for DI swapping, mocking, published API. The interface wins: the class isn't scanned again, so no duplicates. Interface-method attributes do not propagate to the class method.

```csharp
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Linq;
using Betta.Attributes;
using Betta.Interfaces;

[GrasshopperCollection("MyPack", "Maths")]
public class MyPack : IBettaCollection
{
    [GrasshopperMethod("Cube", "x³")]
    public double Cube([GrasshopperParameter("Value", DefaultValue = 2.0)] double x) => x * x * x;

    [GrasshopperMethod("Stats")]
    public (double Sum, double Average) Stats([GrasshopperParameter("Numbers")] List<double> numbers)
        => numbers.Count == 0 ? (0, 0) : (numbers.Sum(), numbers.Average());
}
```

For interface style, move the attributes to `IMyPack : IBettaCollection` and write `class MyPack : IMyPack`.

## Attributes

| Attribute | Target | Members |
|---|---|---|
| `[GrasshopperCollection(category, subCategory)]` | interface/class | default category for every method |
| `[GrasshopperMethod(name, description?)]` | method | `Name`, `NickName`, `Description`, `Category`, `SubCategory`, `IconResource`, `Guid`, `Enabled` |
| `[GrasshopperParameter(name, nickName?, description?)]` | parameter | `Name`, `NickName`, `Description`, `Optional`, `DefaultValue` |

`DefaultValue` must be a compile-time constant (number, string, bool, enum); complex defaults go in the method body. Keep services free of Grasshopper types; `Rhino.Geometry` types are fine.

## Types to inputs/outputs (compressed)

| In code | Becomes |
|---|---|
| Param `T` / `enum` | item input (enum = integer; name string parses) |
| Param `List<T>`, `T[]`, `params T[]` | list input (access inferred from the CLR type; there is no `[Access]`) |
| Param `Line`/`Arc`/`Polyline`/`Circle`/`Surface` | accepted as `Curve` / `Brep` |
| Param `CancellationToken`, `IProgress<T>`, `IBettaReport`, `[GrasshopperMenuState]`/`[GrasshopperSecret]`/`[GrasshopperTrigger]` | no wired pin |
| `throw` in the method / `report.Warning("…")` on an `IBettaReport` param | error, no outputs / warning, outputs still set |
| Param `GH_Structure<TGoo>`, `[GrasshopperValueList]`, `[GrasshopperRange]`/`[GrasshopperNotEmpty]` | tree / auto value list / validated |
| Return primitive, Rhino geometry, `List<T>` | one output / one list output |
| Return `(A a, B b)` or `Tuple<...>` | one output per element |
| Return plain custom class | one output per public property |
| Return opaque class (`[GrasshopperOpaque]`/`IBettaValue`) | one typed wire, no explosion |
| Return `Bitmap`/`Image` | one generic object |
| Return `Task<T>`/`ValueTask<T>`, `IObservable<T>` | async / live streaming component |

### Naming outputs

Priority: (1) `[GrasshopperOutput("Name", "Nick", "tip")]` on the method or `[return: ...]`; for tuples repeat with `Index = 0`, `1`, ...; (2) ValueTuple element names (`(double Sum, double Average)` gives `Sum`/`Average`), so a named tuple is the easy route; (3) defaults: `Output`, `Output1..N`, or property names.

## GUID and save/reload stability

`ComponentGuid` = MD5 of `ServiceType.FullName | Method.Name`. Saved `.gh` files re-match on it across sessions, machines, plugin releases, Rhino updates and .NET versions, provided the plugin DLL is in the Betta folder.

- **Safe (not hashed):** parameters and the return type (add, rename, retype), display `Name`/`NickName`, `Description`, `Category`/`SubCategory`, icon. Like a hand-written `GH_Component` keeping its `ComponentGuid`: files reconnect wires **by position**, so add new inputs and outputs (tuple elements) after the existing ones; inserting or reordering rewires old files wrongly.
- **Renaming changes the GUID**: the method, its class/namespace, or moving the method to another type. Keep saved files working by listing the old name: `[GrasshopperMethod("Map", FormerNames = new[] { "Remap" })]` (a moved method: `"Old.Namespace.OldType.Remap"`), or for a renamed type `[GrasshopperCollection(..., FormerNames = new[] { "Old.Namespace.OldType" })]`. Betta registers each old GUID as a hidden alias; files open and take the new GUID when saved again. No tool needed: you know the old name. To change the subcategory, set `SubCategory` on `[GrasshopperMethod]` instead of moving the method.
- **Overloads:** if a type has two `[GrasshopperMethod]`s with the same method name, both GUIDs also hash the full signature (``Type|Method|paramType name,...|ReturnType``, version-free type names), so any signature change breaks them. Give each component method its own name; the source generator warns (`BETTA011`).
- **`[GrasshopperMethod("Name", Guid = "...")]`** fixes the id for good. Use it to **port a hand-written `GH_Component`** (give the method the old `ComponentGuid`, and existing files open the Betta version). Pinning a published method's *current* GUID before a rename also works; never pin a new random one, which breaks saved files like the rename would. `betta_describe` (Betta.Mcp) reports the current GUID, the `FormerNames` aliases and every GUID Betta.log recorded for the component; the Betta Inspector component shows the live value in Rhino.
- **Before 0.8** the hash covered the whole signature with `Type.FullName`, which for generic signatures (`List<T>`, tuples, `Task<T>`, `IObservable<T>`) also included assembly versions. 0.8 registers that old GUID as a hidden alias: 0.7 files open and take the new GUID on the next save (for generic signatures only if saved with the same plugin, Rhino and .NET versions). `betta_describe` shows it as `legacyGuid`.
- A saved `.gh` showing missing components usually means a renamed or moved method or a missing DLL, not a Betta bug.

## Read when...

- New project, csproj, deploy folder, custom icon (`IconResource`): `references/setup-deploy.md`
- Need the complete mapping table (Color/Guid/Interval/Transform/Box, tuple arity 8+, entitlement row): `references/type-mapping.md`
- Returning `Task<T>`, cancellation, `IProgress`, or `IObservable<T>`: `references/async-streaming.md` (streaming is there)
- Pipeline domain objects, opaque types, viewport preview, bake, `BettaImage`, `IBettaDefault`/`IBettaSerializable`: `references/opaque-preview.md`
- Right-click menu state, secrets, run trigger, value list: `references/ui-inputs.md`
- `GH_Structure` trees, branched inputs, `[GrasshopperRange]`/`[GrasshopperNotEmpty]`/custom validators, errors and warnings from the method body: `references/trees-validation.md`
- Constructor injection, `IBettaModule`, `[GrasshopperRequiresEntitlement]`/`IBettaLicenseGate`: `references/di-licensing.md`
- Debugging registration (Inspector, `Betta_Status`, `Betta.log`), `dotnet new` templates, Betta.Mcp, `betta-docs`, example projects in the repo: `references/tooling-diagnostics.md`

# Opaque domain values, viewport preview, bake, BettaImage

## Opaque domain values (pass-through, no explosion)

By default a method that returns a custom class explodes into one output per public property: convenient for value bags, terrible for pipelines. Mark a class **opaque** to keep it as a single typed wire that another Betta method can accept as a typed input:

```csharp
[GrasshopperOpaque]                  // option A: type attribute
public class FloorplanGraph { ... }

public class FloorplanGraph2 : IBettaValue { ... }   // option B: marker interface

[GrasshopperMethod("Load")]
[return: GrasshopperOpaque]          // option C: per-method override
FloorplanGraphRaw Load(string path); // makes THIS return opaque
                                     // even when the type isn't marked
```

Betta auto-generates a `GH_BettaGoo<T>` + `Param_BettaGoo<T>` pair at discovery time. The `Param_BettaGoo<T>` carries a deterministic `ComponentGuid` = MD5 of `typeof(T).FullName`, so saved `.gh` files survive across rebuilds and machine moves.

A `List<T>` of opaque `T` flows as a single list-access output of the same typed param. No special syntax: Betta strips the list wrapper and reuses the registered factory.

**When to mark opaque:** any domain object you want to pass through a pipeline (Load -> Transform -> Deconstruct). **When not to:** value-bag DTOs whose properties are the useful output.

## Opt-ins for opaque types (recap)

| Marker / interface | Effect |
|---|---|
| `[GrasshopperOpaque]` or `IBettaValue` | Pass through as a single typed wire. |
| `IBettaPreview` (Betta.Preview pkg) | Viewport draw forwarded by the wrapping component. |
| `IBettaBakeable` (Betta.Preview pkg) | Right-click -> Bake adds geometry to the active Rhino doc. |
| `IBettaDefault` | Unwired opaque inputs get a fresh `new T()` instead of `null`. |
| `IBettaSerializable` | Round-trip the value through `.gh` save/reload (bytes-based). |

## Viewport preview (`Betta.Preview`)

Opaque domain objects can opt into Rhino viewport drawing by implementing `IBettaPreview` (package and namespace `Betta.Preview`; `IBettaValue` lives in `Betta.Interfaces`):

```csharp
using Betta.Preview;
using Rhino.Geometry;
using Grasshopper.Kernel;

public class Graph : IBettaValue, IBettaPreview
{
    public BoundingBox ClippingBox => /* union of geometry */ ;
    public void DrawWires(IGH_PreviewArgs args)  => /* args.Display.Draw* */ ;
    public void DrawMeshes(IGH_PreviewArgs args) => /* args.Display.Draw* */ ;
}
```

Betta detects `IBettaPreview` by interface-name string (so the Betta runtime stays free of a hard `Betta.Preview` reference) and the wrapping component automatically advertises `IsPreviewCapable`, sums `ClippingBox`, and forwards Draw calls via reflection. Caching is per-solve and zero-overhead when no return type implements `IBettaPreview`. `IBettaBakeable` (`Bake(RhinoDoc, ObjectAttributes, List<Guid>)`) is detected independently, so a type can bake without previewing.

## BettaImage

A `Bitmap` / `Image` return or parameter becomes a single `Param_GenericObject` (no property explosion). For bake + PNG serialize return `Betta.Preview.BettaImage` (opaque). It is bakeable (PictureFrame, PNG round-trip) but deliberately not `IBettaPreview`.

1	# Async, cancellation, progress, streaming
2	
3	## Async essentials (CancellationToken, IProgress)
4	
5	Methods returning `Task<T>` (or `ValueTask<T>`) are async: the runtime kicks off the task, caches by input hash, and calls `ExpireSolution(true)` on completion. They can take a `CancellationToken` parameter. The runtime synthesizes one per solve and cancels the previous when the component re-solves, so stale work quits cleanly:
6	
7	```csharp
8	[GrasshopperMethod("Slow Sum")]
9	async Task<double> SumAsync(List<double> xs, CancellationToken ct) { ... }
10	```
11	
12	`IProgress<int>` / `IProgress<string>` parameters become a sink that updates the component's `Message` tag, giving users a "computing 42%" indicator for free. Both `CancellationToken` and `IProgress<T>` are synthetic: no input pin.
13	
14	## Streaming (`IObservable<T>`)
15	
16	A method returning `IObservable<T>` becomes a live component. `T` maps to outputs like a normal return (primitive, tuple, opaque, ...).
17	
18	- Betta **subscribes on the first solve** (status shows *listening*); the method runs once per subscription, not once per emission.
19	- Every emission pushes the **newest value** to the output; re-solves are coalesced on the UI thread, so a fast stream can skip intermediate values. Not for lossless event delivery.
20	- **Changing any wired input** disposes the old subscription and re-invokes the method for a new one.
21	- The subscription is disposed when the component leaves the canvas; the `IDisposable` your observable's `Subscribe` returns must really release watchers/timers/sockets.
22	
23	```csharp
24	[GrasshopperMethod("Ticker")]
25	public IObservable<long> Ticker([GrasshopperParameter("Seconds", DefaultValue = 1)] int seconds)
26	    => Observable.Interval(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(seconds));
27	```
28	
29	Betta ships no Rx: using `System.Reactive` means bundling `System.Reactive.dll` next to your plugin DLL. Without it, hand-roll the observable like the `Ticker` in `Betta/Services/SimpleService.cs`.

# Async, cancellation, progress, streaming

## Async essentials (CancellationToken, IProgress)

Methods returning `Task<T>` (or `ValueTask<T>`) are async: the runtime kicks off the task, caches by input hash, and calls `ExpireSolution(true)` on completion. They can take a `CancellationToken` parameter. The runtime synthesizes one per solve and cancels the previous when the component re-solves, so stale work quits cleanly:

```csharp
[GrasshopperMethod("Slow Sum")]
async Task<double> SumAsync(List<double> xs, CancellationToken ct) { ... }
```

`IProgress<int>` / `IProgress<string>` parameters become a sink that updates the component's `Message` tag, giving users a "computing 42%" indicator for free. Both `CancellationToken` and `IProgress<T>` are synthetic: no input pin.

## Streaming (`IObservable<T>`)

A method returning `IObservable<T>` becomes a live component. `T` maps to outputs like a normal return (primitive, tuple, opaque, ...).

- Betta **subscribes on the first solve** (status shows *listening*); the method runs once per subscription, not once per emission.
- Every emission pushes the **newest value** to the output; re-solves are coalesced on the UI thread, so a fast stream can skip intermediate values. Not for lossless event delivery.
- **Changing any wired input** disposes the old subscription and re-invokes the method for a new one.
- The subscription is disposed when the component leaves the canvas; the `IDisposable` your observable's `Subscribe` returns must really release watchers/timers/sockets.

```csharp
[GrasshopperMethod("Ticker")]
public IObservable<long> Ticker([GrasshopperParameter("Seconds", DefaultValue = 1)] int seconds)
    => Observable.Interval(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(seconds));
```

Betta ships no Rx: using `System.Reactive` means bundling `System.Reactive.dll` next to your plugin DLL. Without it, hand-roll the observable like the `Ticker` in `Betta/Services/SimpleService.cs`.

I added two files in a new `Facade` folder:
- **`Facade/Panel.cs`:** the `Panel` class, marked `[GrasshopperOpaque]` so each panel travels on its own "Panel" wire. It holds the four corners, the index, and the outline, area, planarity deviation and center. Width and height (mean of edges 1 and 3, and of edges 2 and 4) are defined here once, so Nest On Sheets and Cut List use the same values.
- **`Facade/FacadePack.cs`:** `IFacadePack` and `FacadePack`, with all 8 components in category "Facade". This follows the existing interface-plus-class style. Subcategories are Panels, Analysis and Fabrication.

Choices I made where the brief was open:
- **Panel order:** panels run along U first, so a panel's index is `v * UCount + u`. Corners go around each cell: (u, v), (u+1, v), (u+1, v+1), (u, v+1).
- **Planarity:** if the first three corners are collinear, the plane is invalid and the deviation counts as 0.
- **Errors and warnings:** errors (bad counts in Panelize Surface, empty Panel Stats, empty Path with Write on in Cut List) are thrown. Warnings (Planarity, Nest On Sheets) go through `IBettaReport`.
- **Nest On Sheets:** it runs off the UI thread, cancels the old run when inputs change, and reports progress as a percentage. A part is turned 90° only if it doesn't fit upright in the current shelf, in a new shelf, or on a fresh sheet. Panels that fit on no sheet are counted and skipped.
- **Cut List:** the CSV uses invariant-culture numbers and `\n` line endings.
